newsitem.title: UK: Hanjin to invest 80 mln marks in DSR-Senator Lines.
newsitem.headline: Hanjin to invest 80 mln marks in DSR-Senator Lines.

text.p: Hanjin Shipping Co Ltd said on Friday it would invest 80 million marks ($43 million) to fund a reorganisation of its German container shipping subsidiary, DSR-Senator Lines GmbH.
The South Korean shipping firm said the investment was part of a 100 million mark recapitalisation of the Bremen-based company.

S.H. Lee, Hanjin Shipping executive vice-president with responsibility for DSR-Senator, told Reuters the investment was part of a group plan to integrate DSR-Senator's operations with those of Hanjin.
Sales operations will remain separate, said Lee, to maintain the two firms' identities with customers.
"We will be making this investment in the next few months," said Lee. "The new funds will be used to reorganise the vessel schedules and the other operations."
He said that after the recapitalisation, the company would have paid up capital of 275 million marks.
The investment would be made in proportion to current shareholdings in DSR-Senator, Lee said.
Hanjin owns 80 percent of the German shipping group, while DSR and the Bremen state-owned investment company Hanseatische Industrie Beteiligungen (Hibeg) hold 10 percent each.
The other two shareholders will invest 10 million marks each, Mr Lee said.
The merger of DSR-Senator with Hanjin Shipping will create a container shipping group operating world-wide with around 100 vessels with a total capacity of 400,000 twenty foot equivalent units (teu).

The new operation is to scrap DSR-Senator Line's round-the-world container service in favour of a range of joint end-to-end routes operated in collaboration with South Korea's Cho Yang Shipping and Kuwait-based United Arab Shipping Company.
DSR-Senator Line offices in Rostock, Singapore, Dubai, San Francisco and Genoa will be closed at the cost of 140 jobs, cutting total staff to around 480.

Hanjin Shipping acquired a majority stake in loss-making DSR-Senator Lines in January, just three years after it was created from the merger of Bremen-based Senator Linie with former East German state shipping line Deutsche Seereederei Rostock. -Julian Bray, Reuters Shipping Desk, +44 171 542 4087/4012 Fax 542 5017 ($ = 1.842 German Marks)
